title: Tenali Raman and the Divine Boon of Laughter

full_text:
In his youth, before he entered the court of Vijayanagara, Tenali was known simply as Ramakrishna, a brilliant but penniless young scholar living in the village of Tenali. Seeking purpose and livelihood, an elderly wandering sage taught him a sacred mantra of the Divine Mother, the fierce celestial guardian, and said:
'Go to the ancient hilltop shrine at midnight. Recite this mantra three million times, and the Divine Mother will appear to grant thee thy destiny.'

Ramakrishna went to the lonely stone shrine. He sat in meditation and chanted with pure devotion through stormy nights and howling winds until his mantra was complete.

Suddenly, a blinding flash of celestial lightning illuminated the sanctum.
The Fierce Guardian Mother manifested before him, majestic and terrifying, possessing a thousand radiant faces and two thousand arms bearing sacred emblems of power!

Any ordinary mortal would have fainted in superstitious dread.
Young Ramakrishna looked up at the thousand faces, then looked down at his own small hands, and suddenly burst into uncontrollable, joyous laughter:
'Ha-ha-ha! Ho-ho-ho!'

The Divine Mother frowned with thunderous astonishment:
'Insolent youth! Mortals tremble in terror before my presence, yet thou dost laugh in my face! What causes thy reckless mirth?'

Ramakrishna bowed low, still chuckling with innocent delight:
'O Blessed Mother of the Universe! Forgive me! I looked at you and was struck by a practical thought:
We poor humans have only one nose, and when we catch a common cold, we struggle with two hands to wipe it with a handkerchief.
I looked at your thousand magnificent faces and two thousand arms, and I thought: "Heavens! If the Mother of the Universe ever catches a cold, how does she manage to wipe a thousand running noses with only two thousand hands?" The picture was so delightfully humorous that I could not hold back my laughter!'

The Fierce Guardian Mother stared at the youth, and her terrifying countenance softened into a radiant, celestial smile. She burst into divine laughter that echoed across the mountains:
'Ramakrishna! Thy fearlessness, thy pure innocence, and thy razor-sharp wit have conquered my heart!
Thou didst not tremble, nor didst thou ask for gold.
Henceforth, thou shalt be known as a *Vikatakavi*—the Supreme Jester-Poet! Thy wit shall outshine the greatest scholars, thy laughter shall humble mighty kings, and thy fame shall endure as long as the stars shine in the heavens!'

Blessed with this divine gift of wit, Tenali Raman journeyed to the imperial court of Vijayanagara, where his humor and wisdom transformed an empire.
moral: Humor, presence of mind, and the courage to find joy even before awe win the favor of destiny.
